clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: Carve it into a doorway. My own pumpkin door. Smells better than oak.
clips.spokenText: Carve it into a doorway. My own pumpkin door. Smells better than oak.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: Oh, now that's the good stuff. My stuffing's all a-flutter.
clips.spokenText: Oh, now that's the good stuff. My stuffing's all a-flutter.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: I've been dying to build a wheelbarrow the size of a pumpkin.
clips.spokenText: I've been dying to build a wheelbarrow the size of a pumpkin.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: The bridge washed out, then the farmer moved on, then... well. Roads forget, if no one walks them.
clips.spokenText: The bridge washed out, then the farmer moved on, then... well. Roads forget, if no one walks them.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: It's not broken, it's... resting.
clips.spokenText: It's not broken, it's... resting.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: Ah. That's a bit... warm, for a fellow made of straw.
clips.spokenText: Ah. That's a bit... warm, for a fellow made of straw.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: Old Crook the chisel. She's chipped, but she knows where the grain wants to go.
clips.spokenText: Old Crook the chisel. She's chipped, but she knows where the grain wants to go.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: You're too good to me. Don't stop.
clips.spokenText: You're too good to me. Don't stop.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: One day, aye. One day I'll let someone help me. Gosh, that sounded brave.
clips.spokenText: One day, aye. One day I'll let someone help me. Gosh, that sounded brave.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: It's a very relaxed door. I'm jealous, honestly.
clips.spokenText: It's a very relaxed door. I'm jealous, honestly.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: There's my favourite farmer. Don't tell the crows.
clips.spokenText: There's my favourite farmer. Don't tell the crows.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: Come in, come in. Well, there's no door. Come near, then.
clips.spokenText: Come in, come in. Well, there's no door. Come near, then.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: People think being made of straw's a nuisance. It's not. I never need a pillow.
clips.spokenText: People think being made of straw's a nuisance. It's not. I never need a pillow.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: I lent it to Mabel for a hat. She made the hat. I made a draught.
clips.spokenText: I lent it to Mabel for a hat. She made the hat. I made a draught.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: We used to get a cart from your side of the hill every week. Pumpkins, apples, gossip.
clips.spokenText: We used to get a cart from your side of the hill every week. Pumpkins, apples, gossip.

clips.speaker: rowan
clips.text: The crows and I have an arrangement. They don't eat my stuffing, I don't flap at them.
clips.spokenText: The crows and I have an arrangement. They don't eat my stuffing, I don't flap at them.

clips.speaker: shane
clips.text: And the neighbours are monsters. Lovely ones, honestly. They wander up the path to buy our pumpkins.
clips.spokenText: And the neighbours are monsters. Lovely ones, honestly. They wander up the path to buy our pumpkins.

clips.speaker: shane
clips.text: The neighbours ask favours too. Nat keeps them in the journal, very neatly. And as the patch levels up, new attractions open.
clips.spokenText: The neighbours ask favours too. Nat keeps them in the journal, very neatly. And as the patch levels up, new attractions open.

clips.speaker: shane
clips.text: Skyla sells them at her stall, and later in our own shop, the Honest Pumpkin. She runs the till. Mostly by sitting on it.
clips.spokenText: Skyla sells them at her stall, and later in our own shop, the Honest Pumpkin. She runs the till. Mostly by sitting on it.
